issue_context.title: [Feature] Use `micromatch` or better for faster file matching
issue_context.body:
This isn't really a feature, but I wasn't sure I should file this as a bug.

Currently, playwright depends on a very old version of `minimatch` (v3) for file matching. 

The file matching operation is done a few times during playwright startup. 
`micromatch` [performs significantly better](https://www.npmjs.com/package/micromatch#running-benchmarks) in glob matching, and this can have a small but noticeable impact on startup times for large projects that use playwright.

I was about to send across a PR for this when I noticed that playwright [uses some API bits](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/b4ffb848de1b00e9a0abad6dacdccce60cce9bed/packages/playwright-test/src/runner/projectUtils.ts#L171-L192) from `minimatch` that aren't compatible with `micromatch`. e.g. Parsing comments in patterns.

Overall, this might _technically_ be a breaking change since there are a few esoteric features like comments in globs that `micromatch` doesn't support (does anyone really use them?), but it is otherwise largely a self-stated replacement for minimatch.
A 3-10x performance jump might justify such a change.
comments: Do you have numbers how much it would improve?

On a large project that I work with, supplying a `glob` pattern in `testPattern` (which causes playwright to use `minimatch`) results in the `collectFiles` playwright test function to take 21 seconds.

The same decrease to 8.5 seconds if we supply a regex to `testPattern` instead (which uses native JS regex `test`).

Now the repo is quite large and we have multiple playwright projects, so the difference is very stark, however, I'd expect the % difference to be nearly the same for normal repos as well.

About how many files are we talking about? We are curious about your project structure, or better if we could have a repro.

How many gitignore files do you have? Did you count how often the minimatch gets called? Since its only used to parse gitignore entries.

I think the actual use of minimatch which is relevant is this one: 

https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/4b1b4dc23bd5e58a0d72e4d083f2a8fb8114fe85/packages/playwright-test/src/util.ts#L138

About 100k files in our monorepo, and 7 different projects.

I don't think the usage for gitignore is problematic. Its perhaps the file matcher here —
https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/v1.36.0/packages/playwright-test/src/util.ts#L108-L143

which is used by a bunch of different other functions.

The performance difference between `minimatch` and `micromatch` is relatively well known as well, with other tools such as Jest making a move —
https://github.com/jestjs/jest/pull/2338
a while back now.
We would be happy to accept a contribution for it, if you want to take over this change, feel free to file a PR, thanks!
